```{r cleaning-function}
# Clean one year of air pollution data.
#
# Arguments:
#   file_path: Path to the original CSV file.
#   ozone_units: Desired ozone units, "ppm" (default) or "ppb".
#                Original ozone concentrations are in ppm.
#
# Returns:
#   A tibble with one row per observed date and columns:
#   date, co, pm25, and o3.
#   Missing concentrations remain NA.

clean_air <- function(file_path, ozone_units = "ppm") {

  ozone_units <- match.arg(ozone_units, c("ppm", "ppb"))

  # Read the original measurements.
  raw <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

  required_columns <- c(
    "Date",
    "Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration",
    "Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration",
    "Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration"
  )

  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(raw))

  if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Missing columns in ", file_path, ": ",
      paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  # Remove exact duplicate source records and rename columns.
  dat <- raw %>%
    distinct() %>%
    transmute(
      date = mdy(.data$Date),
      co = .data[["Daily Max 8-hour CO Concentration"]],
      pm25 = .data[["Daily Mean PM2.5 Concentration"]],
      o3 = .data[["Daily Max 8-hour Ozone Concentration"]]
    )

  if (anyNA(dat$date)) {
    stop("Missing or invalid dates in ", file_path)
  }

  pollutants <- c("co", "pm25", "o3")

  if (!all(vapply(dat[pollutants], is.numeric, logical(1)))) {
    stop("Pollutant columns must contain numeric values: ", file_path)
  }

  # Correct negative measurements before averaging.
  for (pollutant in pollutants) {
    dat[[pollutant]] <- pmax(dat[[pollutant]], 0)
  }

  # Preserve NA if every measurement in a group is missing.
  mean_or_na <- function(x) {
    if (all(is.na(x))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }

  # Calculate daily means for each pollutant.
  dat <- dat %>%
    group_by(date) %>%
    summarise(
      across(all_of(pollutants), mean_or_na),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(date)

  # Convert ozone units when requested.
  if (ozone_units == "ppb") {
    dat <- dat %>%
      mutate(o3 = o3 * 1000)
  }

  return(dat)
}
```

```{r process-data}
# Process all three years using ozone concentrations in ppm.
air2018 <- clean_air("AQ_2018.csv")
air2019 <- clean_air("AQ_2019.csv")
air2020 <- clean_air("AQ_2020.csv")

# Check that each file contains the expected year.
stopifnot(
  all(year(air2018$date) == 2018),
  all(year(air2019$date) == 2019),
  all(year(air2020$date) == 2020)
)

# Combine the cleaned annual datasets.
air <- bind_rows(air2018, air2019, air2020) %>%
  arrange(date) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date)
  )

# Check that dates are unique and concentrations are nonnegative.
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(air$date),
  all(air$co >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  all(air$pm25 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE),
  all(air$o3 >= 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)
```

Processing order affects the results. Removing duplicate records
first prevents them from receiving extra weight in daily averages.
Correcting negative values before averaging also matters:
measurements of -2 and 4 become 0 and 4, giving a daily mean
of 2 rather than 1.


```{r annual-table-function}
# Generate annual minimum and maximum daily concentrations.
make_annual_table <- function(data, selected_year) {

  data %>%
    filter(year == selected_year) %>%
    select(co, pm25, o3) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = everything(),
      names_to = "pollutant",
      values_to = "concentration"
    ) %>%
    group_by(pollutant) %>%
    summarise(
      Minimum = if (all(is.na(concentration))) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        min(concentration, na.rm = TRUE)
      },
      Maximum = if (all(is.na(concentration))) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        max(concentration, na.rm = TRUE)
      },
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Pollutant = case_when(
        pollutant == "co" ~ "CO (ppm)",
        pollutant == "pm25" ~ "PM2.5 (µg/m³)",
        pollutant == "o3" ~ "Ozone (ppm)"
      ),
      pollutant_order = match(
        pollutant,
        c("co", "pm25", "o3")
      )
    ) %>%
    arrange(pollutant_order) %>%
    select(Pollutant, Minimum, Maximum)
}
```

```{r table-2018}
knitr::kable(
  make_annual_table(air, 2018),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Table 1. Minimum and maximum daily concentrations, 2018."
)
```

```{r table-2019}
knitr::kable(
  make_annual_table(air, 2019),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Table 2. Minimum and maximum daily concentrations, 2019."
)
```

```{r table-2020}
knitr::kable(
  make_annual_table(air, 2020),
  digits = 3,
  caption = paste(
    "Table 3. Minimum and maximum daily concentrations,",
    "January–April 2020."
  )
)
```

## Figure 1: Monthly CO and Ozone Concentrations

Daily concentrations were pooled by calendar month across years.
January–April include three years of data, while May–December
include two years.

The 95% confidence intervals were calculated as:

\[
\bar{x} \pm 1.96 \times \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

Here, \(s\) is the standard deviation of daily concentrations,
and \(n\) is the number of days with a non-missing measurement
for the corresponding pollutant and month.

```{r monthly-co-ozone}
# Pool all daily observations for the same calendar month.
monthly_co_o3 <- air %>%
  select(month, co, o3) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(co, o3),
    names_to = "pollutant",
    values_to = "concentration"
  ) %>%
  group_by(month, pollutant) %>%
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(concentration)),
    mean_concentration = if (all(is.na(concentration))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(concentration, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    sd_concentration = sd(concentration, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    se = sd_concentration / sqrt(n),
    lower = mean_concentration - 1.96 * se,
    upper = mean_concentration + 1.96 * se,
    pollutant = factor(
      pollutant,
      levels = c("co", "o3"),
      labels = c("CO (ppm)", "Ozone (ppm)")
    )
  )
```

```{r plot-co-ozone, fig.height=6}
ggplot(
  monthly_co_o3,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = mean_concentration,
    color = pollutant
  )
) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    width = 0.18,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(
    ~pollutant,
    ncol = 1,
    scales = "free_y"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb,
    limits = c(0.5, 12.5)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "CO (ppm)" = "#0072B2",
      "Ozone (ppm)" = "#D55E00"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly CO and Ozone Concentrations",
    subtitle = "Pooled daily means with 95% confidence intervals",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Concentration (ppm)",
    caption = "Jan–Apr: 2018–2020. May–Dec: 2018–2019."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

CO and ozone are shown in separate panels with different y-axis
scales because their concentrations differ substantially.
This makes the monthly pattern of each pollutant easier to see.

## Figure 2: Monthly PM2.5 Concentrations by Year

```{r monthly-pm25}
# Calculate monthly mean PM2.5 separately for each year.
monthly_pm25 <- air %>%
  group_by(year, month) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_pm25 = if (all(is.na(pm25))) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      mean(pm25, na.rm = TRUE)
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r plot-pm25}
ggplot(
  monthly_pm25,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = mean_pm25,
    color = factor(year),
    group = factor(year)
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = 1:12,
    labels = month.abb,
    limits = c(0.5, 12.5)
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c(
      "2018" = "#0072B2",
      "2019" = "#D55E00",
      "2020" = "#009E73"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Monthly Mean PM2.5 Concentrations by Year",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Mean PM2.5 concentration (µg/m³)",
    color = "Year",
    caption = "2020 data are available only through April."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

Lines connect monthly averages to show changes over time, while
points and different colors make comparisons across years easier.

## Interpretation

CO concentrations were generally higher in late fall and winter,
while ozone concentrations were higher in spring and summer.
PM2.5 patterns differed across years, and the highest daily PM2.5
concentration was observed in 2020 at 31.200 µg/m³.
However, 2020 includes only January–April, and the pooled estimates
for May–December are based on two years rather than three.
